title: Exact-v6 exploration and SD-CFR average-strategy control
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Under synchronized common-deck collection, 0.1 opponent exploration will prevent zero-traverser coverage collapse and reduce seat-node imbalance relative to epsilon0, while the correct iteration-weighted per-hand strategy-snapshot policy remains at least directionally competitive on generic anchors.
material_change: Add recorded opponent epsilon mixing to the exact-v6 traversal, store every iteration network with linear-CFR weights, run matched epsilon0/0.1 three-iteration arms, and evaluate the frozen per-hand snapshot-and-action-sampled SD-CFR policy on a common 256-pair three-anchor panel.
baseline: Synchronization alone improved terminal anchors but had worse mean log imbalance 3.960 and zero P0 traverser nodes in iterations 2 and 3; prior evaluations incorrectly centered terminal current networks rather than SD-CFR snapshot mixtures.
notes: Opponent epsilon follows the repository batched Deep CFR behavior-policy mixture and is recorded; no importance correction is claimed. Primary evaluation samples one iteration-weighted snapshot per candidate hand and then samples regret-matched actions.

Post-run primary-source audit: Brown et al. 2019 Algorithm2 samples opponent actions directly from sigma; Algorithm1/Section5.2 trains each player sequentially and reinitializes the value model from scratch each iteration. Source https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/brown19b.html. Earlier sequential-bug diagnosis is superseded; warm updates are the next controlled deviation.

result.summary: Epsilon0.1 reduced mean seat log imbalance from 0.939 to 0.288 and preserved all seat-iteration coverage, but its correct per-hand weighted-snapshot policy was worse on two of three anchors and mean by -220.23 bb/100 versus epsilon0.
result.conclusion: Repository-style epsilon exploration is structurally useful but neither sufficient nor paper-faithful. The average-strategy snapshot contract is retained; the next material contract question is fresh-per-iteration versus warm value-network training.
result.next_step: Run a matched epsilon0 sequential warm-versus-fresh-reinit control with common decks/seeds/buffers and weighted-snapshot evaluation, following Brown et al. Algorithm1/2.
